draft.title: Fees and interest
card: Fees add to what you pay. An account fee is charged for keeping an account, often each month. A late fee is charged when a bill is paid after its due date.

Interest is the cost of borrowing money. Simple interest is worked out on the original amount only. I = P × r × t, where P is the amount, r is the yearly rate as a decimal, and t is the time in years.
Worked example: borrow $2000 at 6% per year for 3 years. I = 2000 × 0.06 × 3 = $360. The total to repay is 2000 + 360 = $2360.
If the time is in months, change it to years first. 6 months is 6 ÷ 12 = 0.5 years.
draft.remember: Fees and interest add to the cost. Simple interest = amount × rate × time in years.

a.q: Sam borrows $1500 at 4% simple interest per year for 2 years. How much interest does he pay?
a.why: I = 1500 × 0.04 × 2 = $120. The answer $60 is for one year only, because the time was left out. $1620 is the total to repay, not the interest.
a.clue: Change 4% to a decimal, then multiply all three numbers.

b.q: Priya borrows $3000 at 5% simple interest per year for 18 months. What is the total she must repay?
b.why: 18 months is 1.5 years. I = 3000 × 0.05 × 1.5 = $225, so the total is 3000 + 225 = $3225. $3150 comes from using 1 year, and $3750 comes from using 18 as the time.
b.clue: Turn 18 months into years before you multiply.

problems.detail: The why says $3750 comes from using 18 as the time, but 3000 × 0.05 × 18 = $2700, which gives a total of $5700. $3750 is not explained by that error, so the explanation is false.

The distractor '$3225.00 per year' repeats the figure in the right answer. Because 3225 appears twice, a student can guess it is the right figure without working it out. The 'per year' version is also more a trick of units than a test of the idea.

check.summary: The card and question a are correct. In question b, the why wrongly says $3750 comes from using 18 as the time (that error gives $5700), and the repeated 3225 figure in the options hints at the answer.
